### `system_dispatch_module_build_batch`

Plan + dispatch a native module-build batch for a base_sha..head_sha range: computes which modules need rebuilding (System::ModuleBuildPlannerService — or every module with force_all), creates the System::ModuleBuildBatch, and leases ephemeral module-forge builders to run each module's ci.module_build task (System::NativeModuleBuildOrchestrator#dispatch!). Returns the batch immediately — planning and the first dispatch pass are synchronous; build/sign/publish completion is tracked asynchronously via the batch's status (see system_list_tasks / system_get_task for the underlying ci.module_build tasks). This planner builds ONLY manifest-backed platform modules (those with a modules/<slug>/ tree); package-origin modules materialized from an upstream apt/rpm package build through a separate package-closure trigger and are never planned here even with force_all — the result lists any it dropped under excluded_modules[] (with a reason each) plus excluded_count, and system_refresh_package_module is how you rebuild those. Requires system.module_builds.dispatch, which core grants explicitly only to the system_worker role by design (bounds a leaked NON-admin token's blast radius) — so ordinary agent/operator principals are denied, but a system.admin holder CAN invoke it (User#has_permission? short-circuits on system.admin, before the role-grant exclusion is consulted). Confirmed live over MCP: an admin operator connector dispatches successfully.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.module_builds.dispatch

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `base_sha` | string | Yes | - | Pre-push commit SHA (diff base) the planner compares from |
| `head_sha` | string | Yes | - | Post-push commit SHA (diff head); also the source of each build's short tag |
| `force_all` | boolean | No | - | Skip the diff and plan every module with a manifest (manual full rebuild / CVE-driven sweep). Default false. |
| `trigger` | string | No | `push`, `manual`, `cve`, `package` | push \| manual \| cve \| package (default manual) — recorded on the batch for audit |
| `source_repo` | string | No | - | "<owner>/<repo>" the base_sha..head_sha diff is taken against (default: the ci_build_source_repo manifest repo). Pass the CORE repo (e.g. powernode/powernode-platform) for a core-change build so the planner diffs the tree the change actually lives in. Getting this wrong can no longer plan 0 silently: the shas are usually absent from the other repo (the compare fails and the error names the repo it diffed), and a core range whose paths match no CORE_PATH_MODULES rule now raises rather than reporting a successful build of nothing. A core range touching only docs/CI hygiene still plans 0 legitimately. |

### `system_cancel_module_build_batch`

Stop a running native module-build batch. This is the operator kill switch: it transitions the batch to `cancelled`, cancels every member ci.module_build task that has not already finished, releases the builder leases those tasks held, and — critically — prevents the orchestrator from leasing a builder for any still-queued module. Cancelling a single task via system_cancel_task does NOT stop a batch: the orchestrator advances on every task completion and simply dispatches the next queued module onto a fresh builder. Already-published module versions are NOT rolled back (a batch that published before you cancelled it has already promoted those versions — use the module rollback path for that); this stops further building only. Refuses when the batch has already reached a terminal state.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.module_builds.cancel

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `batch_id` | string | Yes | - | System::ModuleBuildBatch id to cancel |
| `reason` | string | No | - | Operator-supplied reason, recorded on the batch's error_message for audit |

### `system_rollback_module_version`

Repoint a module's current_version back to an earlier version after a bad publish — the undo for auto-promotion, and the forward-repoint when a good build was withheld. Publishing auto-promotes by DEFAULT, but not unconditionally: promotion is withheld when the module sets auto_promote false, when the artifact is below the non-empty floor, or when System::CoreProvenanceGate refuses its core provenance — each emits a high-severity system.module_promotion_withheld event naming the reason. So a build that completed while current_version_number did not move is not necessarily a promote bug: read that event FIRST. Passing an explicit version_id newer than the current one is the supported way to advance the fleet onto a version that was published but withheld. With version_id, rolls back to that specific version; without it, auto-selects the most recent version that is actually USABLE. That distinction is load-bearing: the version immediately preceding a bad build often carries oci_digest null (it was never published), so a naive roll-back-one would point the fleet at something the agent cannot mount — this walks back until it finds a version with a real artifact that also clears the non-empty floor. Refuses when no usable target exists, when the named version has no usable artifact, or when it belongs to another module. Note this changes which version the fleet RUNS; it does not delete or unpublish the bad version, and nodes converge on their next reconcile.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.modules.rollback

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `module_id` | string | Yes | - | System::NodeModule id to roll back |
| `version_id` | string | No | - | Explicit System::NodeModuleVersion to roll back to. Omit to auto-select the most recent usable version. |
| `reason` | string | No | - | Operator-supplied reason, recorded in the log line for audit |

### `system_gitops_register_repository`

Register a new GitopsRepository pointing at a git remote whose contents describe desired fleet state. The reconciler clones + pulls every 5 min by default; operator can trigger immediately via system_gitops_sync_repository. APPROVAL-GATED (system.gitops_register_repository): when policy requires approval this returns {pending: true} with an approval_request_id and NO repository is registered until an operator approves — do not report a registered repository on that response.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.modules.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Display name (must be unique within the account; max 64 chars) |
| `repo_url` | string | Yes | - | HTTPS or SSH URL. Inline credentials (user:pass@) rejected — use vault_credential_path. |
| `branch` | string | No | - | Default 'main' |
| `vault_credential_path` | string | No | - | Vault KV path with deploy-key + username/password |
| `path_prefix` | string | No | - | Relative path within the repo where fleet.yaml lives (default: repo root) |
| `auto_apply` | boolean | No | - | When true, approved proposals auto-apply on next reconcile (Phase 6b). Default false. |

### `system_gitops_sync_repository`

Trigger an immediate reconcile run for a registered repository. Creates a GitopsSyncRun row + opens proposals for any diffs found. The reconcile runs SYNCHRONOUSLY — `diff_count`, `proposal_ids` and `diff_summary` are already final when this returns, so there is nothing to poll for. Returns `sync_run_id`: the id of the GitopsSyncRun this call finalized, for passing to system_gitops_get_sync_run to re-read the full record (timings, diff_summary, error_message) later. A reconcile that FAILED (clone/pull refused, fleet.yaml did not parse, diff raised) returns success: false with the reason in `error` and the same fields — sync_run_id included — under `data`; do not conclude the fleet matches the repository on that response. When this control plane is not permitted to actuate — standby: not elected, or the quorum gate itself errored — the call refuses BEFORE starting the reconcile: success: false, refusal_code `standby_control_plane`, retryable: false (a retry against THIS plane cannot succeed), and no sync run is created. A success response carries a non-nil `error` only for a `partial` run, where the per-tick proposal cap truncated the proposal set (diff_count exceeds proposal_ids.length).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SystemFleetTool`
- **Permission**: system.modules.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | - | GitopsRepository id |

### `system_gitops_apply_proposal`

NOTE: `publicly_reachable` is the HUB-ELECTION flag — a peer carrying it becomes a hub other peers dial, whose compiled view carries their user devices, and which acts as a BGP route reflector. ### `system_sdwan_propose_federation_peer`

Propose a new federation peer. Status starts at 'proposed'. Approval-gated (sdwan.federation_peer_propose) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and no peer row exists until an operator approves. Acceptance-token minting is NOT available on this surface — a tool result reaches the model provider, so the plaintext cannot be delivered here. To obtain the single-use acceptance token for the Phase 11b handshake, the operator proposes over the REST API (POST /api/v1/system/sdwan/federation_peers), which mints by default and reveals the plaintext once in the approval decision response.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `remote_instance_url` | string | Yes | - | Base URL of the remote Powernode instance to peer with |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | - | Optional identifier of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | - | Optional identifier of the remote account on the peer instance |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | - | /48\|/56\|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `generate_token` | boolean | No | - | Not supported on this surface — passing true is refused with the operator path to use instead. Omit it to propose the peer. |

### `system_sdwan_accept_federation_peer`

Transition a proposed federation peer to accepted. Approval-gated (sdwan.federation_peer_accept) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and the peer is accepted only once an operator approves. When the proposing operator generated a single-use acceptance token, pass it as acceptance_token — it is verified (digest match + not expired + single-use) before the request is gated, and again before the transition is written. Performs the status transition only (sets signed_at + audit metadata); it does NOT run the enroll / node-enrollment / SDWAN-attach chain — that is the federation_acceptance skill.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the federation peer to accept (must be in 'proposed' status) |
| `acceptance_token` | string | No | - | Single-use token supplied by the proposing-account operator, who obtains it over the REST propose path (POST /api/v1/system/sdwan/federation_peers) — it cannot be minted on this MCP surface. Verified against the stored digest; consumed on success. |

### `system_sdwan_update_federation_peer`

Update a federation peer's mutable fields. When `status` is supplied it is gated by the v1 transition matrix (FederationPeer#can_transition_to?) — disallowed transitions return an error. The two trust-boundary transitions are approval-gated exactly as on the REST surface: status 'accepted' routes through sdwan.federation_peer_accept (a peer carrying an acceptance token digest requires acceptance_token, verified up front) and status 'revoked' routes through sdwan.federation_peer_revoke (reason recorded on the peer); under require_approval these return pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and nothing changes until an operator approves. Other transitions apply inline. Mirrors the FederationPeersController#update permitted keys.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the federation peer to update |
| `status` | string | No | - | Target status — must be an allowed v1 transition from the current status. 'accepted' and 'revoked' are approval-gated; other transitions apply inline |
| `acceptance_token` | string | No | - | Single-use token from the proposing-account operator — required when transitioning to 'accepted' on a peer that carries an acceptance token digest. Verified before the request is gated; consumed on success. |
| `reason` | string | No | - | Human-readable revocation reason, recorded on the peer when transitioning to 'revoked' |
| `remote_instance_url` | string | No | - | Base URL of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_instance_id` | string | No | - | Identifier of the remote Powernode instance |
| `remote_account_id` | string | No | - | Identifier of the remote account on the peer instance |
| `remote_prefix_advertisement` | string | No | - | /48\|/56\|/64 ULA prefix the remote instance claims |
| `signed_at` | string | No | - | ISO8601 timestamp marking when the peering was signed |
| `expires_at` | string | No | - | ISO8601 timestamp marking when the peering expires |
| `metadata` | object | No | - | Free-form metadata hash stored on the peer |

### `system_sdwan_revoke_federation_peer`

Revoke a federation peer (terminal in v1) — cuts cross-instance routing, and federated traffic stops immediately. Approval-gated (sdwan.federation_peer_revoke) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and nothing is cut until an operator approves. Same category and executor as system_sdwan_update_federation_peer with status 'revoked', so one approval policy covers both routes to a revoked peer on this tool.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the federation peer to revoke |
| `reason` | string | No | - | Optional human-readable revocation reason (recorded on the peer) |

### `system_sdwan_set_data_residency`

Set a federation peer's data residency region tag (the system_federation_peers.data_residency column, a scalar string ≤64 chars). Used by the residency enforcer to gate which peers may home a given record, so this is a compliance declaration rather than a label. Approval-gated (sdwan.federation_peer_data_residency, seeded require_approval like the propose/accept/revoke trust-boundary verbs) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and the tag is rewritten only once an operator approves. The applied change is recorded on the peer's own audit trail as a federation.peer.data_residency_changed event, readable through system_sdwan_get_audit_log. Also writable by an operator through PATCH /sdwan/federation_peers/:id, under the same gate.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the federation peer to tag |
| `data_residency` | string | Yes | - | Region/residency tag, e.g. 'us-east' or 'eu' |

### `system_sdwan_get_audit_log`

Read-only audit trail for a federation peer: WORM audit shipments (P9.2 sealed FleetEvent batches) plus recent federation.* FleetEvents pertaining to this peer. The events list is a FILTERED operator view (kind federation.* only); the sealed WORM archive captures ALL events referencing the peer regardless of kind and is the complete compliance record. Secret fields (sealed_path, error_message) are not surfaced.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `federation_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the federation peer whose audit trail to read |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max rows per collection (default 50) |

### `system_sdwan_federation_compose`

Stand up a federation overlay topology (hub-and-spoke OR full-mesh) across instances. Creates one Sdwan::Network, enrolls each member as a peer (hubs publicly_reachable), and compiles the per-peer WireGuard + FRR route-policy envelope (Sdwan::PeerEnroller + TopologyCompiler + RoutePolicyCompiler). Failures are collected, not short-circuited.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.federation.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |

| `peers` | array<object> | Yes | - | Member descriptors (1-200). Each: {node_instance_id (required), role: 'hub'\|'spoke' (hub_and_spoke only; default spoke), endpoint_host_v6, endpoint_host_v4, endpoint_port, listen_port, lan_subnets: [cidr], bgp_route_reflector_client: bool} |
| `routing_protocol` | string | No | `static`, `ibgp` | static (default) \| ibgp — 'ibgp' enables FRR route-policy distribution |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | - | Plan only — no rows persisted |

### `system_sdwan_create_virtual_ip`

Create a Virtual IP. Static mode (anycast=false) = single primary holder + ordered failover. Anycast mode (slice 9c iBGP) = all holders advertise simultaneously. CIDR is typically /32 (v4) or /128 (v6). Approval-gated (sdwan.virtual_ip_create) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and the VIP is allocated only once an operator approves.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.vips.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `network_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the SDWAN network the Virtual IP lives in |
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Display name for the Virtual IP |
| `cidr` | string | Yes | - | Host CIDR for the VIP (typically /32 for v4, /128 for v6) within the network's /64 |
| `holder_peer_ids` | array<string> | Yes | - | Ordered: first entry is primary holder when anycast=false. |
| `failover_holder_peer_ids` | array<string> | No | - | Ordered failover candidates (non-anycast); head is promoted on failover |
| `anycast` | boolean | No | - | When true, all holders advertise simultaneously (slice 9c iBGP); default false |
| `description` | string | No | - | Free-form description of the VIP's purpose |
| `tags` | array<string> | No | - | Optional list of tag strings applied to the VIP |
| `advertised_med` | integer | No | - | BGP MULTI_EXIT_DISC advertised for this VIP (default 0) |
| `advertised_local_pref` | integer | No | - | BGP LOCAL_PREF advertised for this VIP (default 100) |

### `system_sdwan_create_port_mapping`

Create a hub DNAT mapping. Exactly one of target_peer_id or target_virtual_ip_id must be set. The hub peer must be in the same network as the target.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.port_mappings.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `network_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the SDWAN network the mapping belongs to |
| `hub_peer_id` | string | Yes | - | UUID of the hub peer that listens for and DNATs the traffic |
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Display name for the port mapping |
| `listen_port` | integer | Yes | - | Port the hub listens on for inbound traffic |
| `protocol` | string | Yes | `tcp`, `udp` | tcp \| udp |
| `target_peer_id` | string | No | - | UUID of the target peer to DNAT to (mutually exclusive with target_virtual_ip_id) |
| `target_virtual_ip_id` | string | No | - | UUID of the target virtual IP to DNAT to (mutually exclusive with target_peer_id) |
| `target_port` | integer | No | - | Defaults to listen_port if omitted |
| `description` | string | No | - | Free-form description of the mapping |
| `enabled` | boolean | No | - | Whether the mapping is active (default true) |
| `metadata` | object | No | - | Free-form operator metadata stored on the mapping |
| `rate_limit` | integer | No | - | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): max NEW CONNECTIONS per second (conntrack flows — the nat chain only sees each connection's first packet, so this throttles connection-establishment rate, not request/packet throughput). Omit for unrestricted (default). |
| `max_connections` | integer | No | - | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): max concurrent connections before excess are dropped. Omit for unrestricted (default). |
| `source_cidrs` | array<string> | No | - | Hardened DNAT tier (increment 6): allow-list of source CIDR strings (v4 and/or v6). Traffic from any other source is dropped. Omit/empty for unrestricted (default). |

Pass rate_limit/max_connections as null or source_cidrs as [] to clear back to unrestricted. |

### `system_sdwan_get_host_bridge`

Fetch a single HostBridge by id, including its lifecycle timestamps. Use this before activate/release rather than paging the whole account list — `state` is what those two verbs turn on (`pending` is invisible to the compiler; `draining` is already on its way out).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.host_bridges.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|

### `system_sdwan_activate_host_bridge`

Mark a HostBridge as `active` so the topology compiler picks it up. Newly allocated bridges land in `pending`; the resolver only sees active bridges. Use this after create_host_bridge when the agent isn't yet reporting back its applied state.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.host_bridges.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | - | Sdwan::HostBridge id |

### `system_sdwan_release_host_bridge`

Release a HostBridge via Sdwan::HostBridgeAllocator.release!. DEFAULTS TO DRAINING: the bridge moves to `draining`, stays in the compiler's `compilable` set and keeps its short_id reserved so in-flight taps finish cleanly. Pass `force: true` to skip that grace window and mark the bridge `removed` immediately — the compiler stops emitting it at once and anything mid-provision against it loses its bridge name. The REST twin (DELETE /api/v1/system/sdwan/host_bridges/:id) carries the same default and the same opt-in. Approval-gated (sdwan.host_bridge_delete) — under require_approval this returns pending: true with a deferred_operation_id and the release happens only once an operator approves.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.host_bridges.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Yes | - | Sdwan::HostBridge id |
| `force` | boolean | No | - | When true, skip the draining grace window and mark removed immediately (default false) |

| `settings` | object | No | - | Free-form settings hash |

Create an OVN logical switch port. `kind` drives compiler choices: vm | container = host-backed (host_node_instance_id required for proper placement); external = uplink/transit (no host required, gets lsp-set-type localnet by default). MAC is auto-generated (locally-administered `02:` prefix) when blank.

| `host_node_instance_id` | string | No | - | Required for vm/container ports; ignored for external |
| `addresses` | array<string> | No | - | Array of IPv4/IPv6 strings; appended to the OVN `addresses=` line |
| `mac` | string | No | - | MAC in `xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx` form; auto-generated when blank |

### `system_sdwan_activate_ovn_logical_switch`

Mark an OvnLogicalSwitch as `active` so the compiler's `compilable` scope picks it up. | `logical_switch_id` | string | Yes | - | Sdwan::OvnLogicalSwitch id |

### `system_sdwan_create_ovn_acl`

Create an OVN ACL (firewall rule) on a logical switch. ACLs operate at the intra-host / logical-network scope (compiled to OVS OpenFlow via OVN's logical-flow translation) — distinct from SDWAN nftables firewall rules which operate at inter-peer scope. Heavyweight-profile only in effect.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.ovn.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `logical_switch_id` | string | Yes | - | Sdwan::OvnLogicalSwitch id this ACL applies to |
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Operator-chosen name (unique per switch, max 63 chars, [letters/digits/_/-/.] only) |
| `direction` | string | Yes | `from-lport`, `to-lport` | from-lport (egress from source pod/VM) \| to-lport (ingress to destination) |
| `priority` | integer | No | - | 0-32767, higher first; default 1000. Ties broken by lexicographic match-string order. |
| `match` | string | Yes | - | OVN match expression, e.g. `ip4.src == 10.0.0.0/8 && tcp.dst == 5432`. Raw OVN syntax — OVN's parser rejects bad values at apply time. |
| `acl_action` | string | Yes | `allow`, `drop`, `reject`, `allow-related` | allow \| drop \| reject \| allow-related |

### `system_sdwan_list_ovn_acls`

List OVN ACLs for the current account, one page at a time, highest priority first. Optionally filter by logical_switch_id (per-switch scope) or sdwan_ovn_deployment_id (per-deployment scope). With no filter, pages through ACLs across every switch in every deployment; read count and has_more to tell a complete answer from a truncated one. ACLs of every state are listed, and at equal priority this order is the UUIDv7 id, NOT the compiler's name tiebreak — use system_sdwan_compile_ovn_plan for OVN evaluation order.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::SdwanTool`
- **Permission**: system.sdwan.ovn.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `logical_switch_id` | string | No | - | Restrict to ACLs on this switch |
| `sdwan_ovn_deployment_id` | string | No | - | Restrict to ACLs on switches under this deployment |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Maximum rows in this page. Omit for the operator-configured default page size. A value above the configured maximum is clamped down, not refused. |
| `cursor` | string | No | - | Opaque keyset cursor taken from a previous page's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page. Read `count` (the total matching your filters, NOT this page's size) and `has_more` to tell a complete answer from a truncated one. |

Translate a natural-language utterance into a structured Project Brief. When mission_id is omitted, creates a new infrastructure mission bound to the system_provisioning template. When mission_id is provided, treats the utterance as a clarification and merges fields onto the existing brief. Returns the brief plus the list of fields still missing for plan composition.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: ai.missions.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | No | - | Existing infrastructure mission ID — omit to create a new one |
| `natural_language` | string | Yes | - | Operator's natural-language description of what they want to provision |
| `prior_brief` | object | No | - | Optional existing brief to merge new fields onto (auto-loaded from mission.configuration['brief'] when mission_id is given) |

### `platform_provisioning_compose_plan`

Run the LLM goal-decomposition kernel against the mission's brief and produce a persisted Ai::GoalPlan whose steps are rewritten into provisioning_skill shape. Returns the DAG plus M1 enrichments: cost_estimate (CostEstimatorService), topology_preview (TopologyRendererService), and risk (RiskScorerService).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: ai.missions.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | - | Infrastructure mission ID |

### `platform_provisioning_approve_plan`

Operator decision on a composed plan. decision='approved' advances the mission past the review_plan gate; 'rejected' sends it back to compose_plan via rejection_mappings; 'modified' applies inline edits to the plan steps before approving. The optional approval_request_id field in the response is reserved for M1 when this routes through the formal approval pipeline.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: ai.missions.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `plan_id` | string | Yes | - | Ai::GoalPlan ID returned by compose_plan |
| `decision` | string | Yes | - | One of: approved, rejected, modified |
| `modifications` | object | No | - | Optional plan-step edits to apply when decision='modified' (shape: { steps: [{ step_number: Int, skill: String }] }) |

### `platform_provisioning_status`

Snapshot of provisioning progress: mission phase, currently-executing step number, and step-number lists by status (completed, pending, failed). For live streaming subscribe to MissionChannel rather than polling this.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: ai.missions.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | - | Infrastructure mission ID |

### `platform_provisioning_adapt`

Propose an adaptation to a live infrastructure mission. Composes a diff-shaped Ai::GoalPlan (only the steps that change) via Ai::Provisioning::AdaptationProposerService, then puts it through the fleet approval gate as action_type project.adapt_<change_type> — the same queue the sensor-driven proposals use — so the operator's intervention policies decide between immediate application and require-approval. Returns the plan id, its steps, and an explicit gate disposition — one of: `routed` (a gate holds it for a decision; nothing ran), `auto_apply_within_bounds` (applied — the steps were appended onto the mission's live plan and dispatched), `parked_gate_unavailable` (no gate could answer; the plan stays in draft and NOTHING ran), `applied_dispatch_failed` (the steps WERE appended but none was enqueued — re-run this action to dispatch them), or `already_applied` (the steps are appended and a run is in flight or finished; re-running does nothing).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ProvisioningTool`
- **Permission**: ai.missions.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `mission_id` | string | Yes | - | Infrastructure mission ID |
| `change_type` | string | Yes | - | One of: scale_horizontal, cost_control, relocate, schema_change, security_change. NOTE: `cost_control` scales the project IN — it composes a `remove_replicas` step that TERMINATES the newest replicas of this mission. Removals are never applied unattended: the plan is always handed to the gate as not auto-apply-eligible, so expect `routed` on the first call. It becomes `auto_apply_within_bounds` only on a later re-run, after a person has approved the request. |
| `metric` | string | No | - | Optional metric that motivated the change (e.g. p99_latency_ms) |
| `details` | object | No | - | Optional structured payload merged into the adaptation signal (observed, target, breach_pct, target_usd, correlation_id, …). For scale_horizontal, include `replica_count` — the fleet's CURRENT replica count. The sensor supplies it on autonomous signals, but an operator-initiated request has no sensor, and the proposer declines rather than assuming the declared size. For cost_control, `breach_pct` sizes the removal — at or above 50 it removes 2 replicas, otherwise 1. |
| `proposed_change` | object | No | - | Legacy envelope: { change_type\|kind: String, …details }. Explicit change_type/metric/details take precedence. |

### `cancel_gitea_workflow_run`

Attempt to cancel a queued or in-progress run. USUALLY FAILS: Gitea exposes no cancel endpoint through 1.27.0, so this returns unsupported=true with an explanation on those versions — it is attempted rather than hardcoded so a future Gitea that adds cancel starts working with no code change. Do NOT route a 'stop this run' request here expecting it to succeed; the run must finish, be discarded via delete_gitea_workflow_run (destructive, and does not stop a running job), or be stopped by tearing down its CI runner.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::GiteaActionsTool`
- **Permission**: devops.ci.write

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `owner` | string | Yes | - | Repository owner — the user or organization login that owns the repo |
| `repo` | string | Yes | - | Repository name (without the owner/ prefix) |
| `run_id` | string | Yes | - | Gitea Actions workflow run ID (from list_gitea_workflow_runs) |

### `delete_gitea_workflow_run`

DESTRUCTIVE: discard a workflow run and its logs. This is NOT a cancel — it does not stop a running job, and the run's logs are unrecoverable afterwards. Gitea exposes no cancel API, so this is the only run-level mutation available; use it only when you actually want the record gone.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::GiteaActionsTool`
- **Permission**: devops.ci.write

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `owner` | string | Yes | - | Repository owner — the user or organization login that owns the repo |
| `repo` | string | Yes | - | Repository name (without the owner/ prefix) |
| `run_id` | string | Yes | - | Gitea Actions workflow run ID to delete |

### `create_gitea_user_token`

Mint a scoped personal access token for the authenticated Gitea user and write it straight into a repo's Gitea Actions secrets. The plaintext is NOT returned — a tool result is persisted with the conversation and forwarded to the model provider, and Gitea cannot re-show a PAT afterwards, so there is no recovery path. set_as_secret is therefore REQUIRED; without it the call refuses before minting anything. Reference the token in the workflow as ${{ secrets.<secret_name> }}.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::GiteaActionsTool`
- **Permission**: devops.ci.write

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `token_name` | string | Yes | - | Human-readable name for the token (e.g. 'platform-ci-readonly') |
| `scopes` | array<string> | No | - | Gitea scope strings (default: ['read:repository']). Common: read:repository, write:repository, read:user, write:user, write:package |
| `set_as_secret` | object | Yes | - | REQUIRED delivery target — the minted token is written here instead of being returned. Hash: {owner, repo, secret_name}. Gitea reserves GITEA_*/GITHUB_* secret names, so pick another (e.g. PLATFORM_READ_TOKEN). |

### `list_gitea_user_tokens`

List the authenticated user's personal access tokens (names + scopes only — plaintext is never returned by Gitea after creation)

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::GiteaActionsTool`
- **Permission**: devops.ci.write
- **Parameters**: none

### `delete_gitea_user_token`

Delete a personal access token by name or numeric ID. Used for rotation or cleanup.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::GiteaActionsTool`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `name_or_id` | string | Yes | - | Token name or numeric ID (from list_gitea_user_tokens) |

### `provision_disk_image_webhook`

Create a per-pipeline disk-image webhook for the current account. Returns the webhook id + absolute URL. The plaintext secret is NOT returned on this surface — a tool result is persisted with the conversation and forwarded to the model provider. The webhook is inert until you fetch a secret: POST /api/v1/system/disk_image_webhooks/<id>/rotate_secret (separate permission; approval-gated — if it answers pending, the plaintext is revealed once in the HTTP approval-decision response, so approve via the operator UI/API, not via approve_deferred_operation). Or use bootstrap_disk_image_ci, which writes the secret straight into the repo's Gitea Actions secrets without returning it.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DiskImageOperatorTool`
- **Permission**: system.platforms.publish_disk_image

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `label` | string | Yes | - | Operator-chosen identifier (unique per account, e.g. 'main-ci', 'release-pipeline') |

### `provision_ci_worker`

Create a per-pipeline CI worker (narrowly scoped: system.platforms.publish_disk_image only). Returns the worker id + roles. The plaintext token is NOT returned on this surface — a tool result is persisted with the conversation and forwarded to the model provider. Obtain the token exactly once via POST /api/v1/system/ci_workers/<id>/rotate_token (ungated, separate permission), or use bootstrap_disk_image_ci, which writes it straight into the repo's Gitea Actions secrets without returning it.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DiskImageOperatorTool`
- **Permission**: system.platforms.publish_disk_image

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Operator-chosen name (e.g. 'release-pipeline-runner') |
| `description` | string | No | - | Optional description shown in the operator UI |

### `bootstrap_disk_image_ci`

End-to-end setup: provision webhook + CI worker, set all 4 needed Gitea Actions secrets in one call (POWERNODE_DISK_IMAGE_WEBHOOK_URL, POWERNODE_DISK_IMAGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POWERNODE_CI_WORKER_TOKEN, POWERNODE_API_BASE). Optionally also mints a Gitea PAT and sets it as PLATFORM_READ_TOKEN for the parent platform checkout step. Idempotent: re-running with the same label rotates secrets + token.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DiskImageOperatorTool`
- **Permission**: system.platforms.publish_disk_image

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `owner` | string | Yes | - | Gitea repo owner |
| `repo` | string | Yes | - | Gitea repo name |
| `label` | string | Yes | - | Operator-chosen identifier (used for both webhook label and CI worker name) |
| `platform_api_base` | string | No | - | Public-routable platform API base URL CI runners will call back to (default: ENV['POWERNODE_PUBLIC_URL'] or 'http://localhost:3000') |
| `create_platform_read_token` | boolean | No | - | When true (default false), mint a Gitea PAT with read:repository scope and set it as PLATFORM_READ_TOKEN secret in the same repo. Closes the manual 'go to Gitea web UI to generate a PAT' step. |
| `platform_read_token_name` | string | No | - | Override the auto-generated PAT name (default: '<label>-platform-ci-readonly') |

### `update_ralph_loop`

Update mutable Ralph Loop config: name, default_agent_id, cycle_interval_minutes, max_iterations_per_day, max_iterations, schedule_paused, max_concurrent_claims. Useful for repointing default_agent_id when consolidating duplicate agents, adjusting cadence without delete+recreate, raising a loop's lifetime iteration cap before it halts on max_iterations_reached, or letting one driver hold several claims at once.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::RalphLoopTool`
- **Permission**: ai.loops.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `loop_id` | string | Yes | - | Ralph loop ID or name |
| `name` | string | No | - | New loop name |
| `default_agent_id` | string | No | - | Repoint to a different agent (UUID, slug, or name) |
| `cycle_interval_minutes` | integer | No | - | Time between iterations in minutes |
| `max_iterations_per_day` | integer | No | - | Daily iteration cap |
| `max_iterations` | integer | No | - | Lifetime iteration cap (distinct from the daily max_iterations_per_day throttle) |
| `schedule_paused` | boolean | No | - | Pause/resume scheduling without a state machine event |
| `max_concurrent_claims` | integer | No | - | How many tasks ONE driver may hold in_progress at once (default 1). Above 1, dev_next_task additionally refuses a task whose metadata.files collide with another in-flight claim, so parallel holders never edit the same file. Set 1 to restore strict single-claim behaviour. |

Use when more work needs to be queued onto a loop that already finished draining.

### `dev_next_task`

Claim the next pending task from a Ralph Loop queue (priority/dependency ordered), or a SPECIFIC pending task with task_key. Returns the task with acceptance criteria, guardrails, and loop context. Idempotent: re-claiming returns your own in-progress task. Refuses when the loop is halted (kill switch, paused, terminal, max iterations).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DevLoopTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `loop_id` | string | Yes | - | Ralph loop ID or name |
| `task_key` | string | No | - | Claim THIS pending task (key or task UUID) instead of the queue head. Applies every guard the positional claim applies and refuses loudly rather than falling back: a task held by another claimant is NOT stolen, and no other task is ever handed back in its place. |
| `holder` | string | No | - | Driver identity (lease holder). For a campaign loop the single-driver lease gates pulls — pass the same holder you claimed the campaign with; the pull renews the lease so another driver can't race in. |

### `dev_complete_task`

Report the outcome of a claimed (in_progress) task, OR resolve a blocked task (operator disposition — no re-claim needed). Records a RalphIteration with verification evidence, transitions the task (passed/failed/blocked/skipped), and captures learnings on the loop.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DevLoopTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `loop_id` | string | Yes | - | Ralph loop ID or name |
| `task_key` | string | Yes | - | Task key being reported |
| `outcome` | string | Yes | - | passed \| failed \| blocked \| skipped |
| `summary` | string | Yes | - | What was done / why it failed, blocked, or was skipped |
| `check_results` | object | No | - | Verification evidence. DECLARE it to get automatic credit: {"evidence": {"framework": "rspec", "passed": 173, "failed": 0, "command": "bundle exec rspec …"}} — an array for several suites. A declared block is adjudicated on its own fields alone (surrounding gate/lint summaries are ignored, so they can neither credit nor contradict it) and ALL declared suites must be green — so declare only the FINAL green runs and keep a red-first run in a plain key beside it, never inside evidence. Anything else is INFERRED by parsing: it still records a pass, but will NOT auto-apply the linked improvement offer (the response says which via evidence_source). |
| `claim_if_pending` | boolean | No | - | Record work finished OUT OF BAND: atomically claim task_key if it is still pending and close it in the same transaction, so an interrupted executor can never strand it in_progress. Refuses rather than steals a task held by another claimant. A `passed` outcome on this path REQUIRES declared check_results.evidence — the platform never saw the claim, so inferred evidence is not enough to close it. |
| `learning` | string | No | - | Reusable learning extracted from this task |
| `git_branch` | string | No | - | Branch the work was committed to |
| `commit_sha` | string | No | - | Commit SHA for the passed task |
| `files_changed` | array<string> | No | - | Paths touched by this task |

### `dev_list_tasks`

List tasks in a Ralph Loop queue, optionally filtered by status (pending | in_progress | passed | failed | blocked | skipped). Use to inspect blocked tasks awaiting disposition or audit the queue. Ordered by position then priority.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DevLoopTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `loop_id` | string | Yes | - | Ralph loop ID or name |
| `status` | string | No | - | Filter by status: pending \| in_progress \| passed \| failed \| blocked \| skipped (omit for all) |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max tasks to return (default 50, max 200) |

### `dev_update_task`

Amend a queued task's brief or routing AFTER it was created — the seam for a decision the operator made post-approval (scope narrowed, one of two offered directions chosen). Edits reach the executor on the next dev_next_task claim. Overwrites are journalled with their prior value in metadata.operator_edits; `note` appends without touching the brief. Cannot change status — use dev_complete_task for transitions.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DevLoopTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.update

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `loop_id` | string | Yes | - | Ralph loop ID or name |
| `task_key` | string | Yes | - | Task key (or task UUID) to amend |
| `note` | string | No | - | Append an attributed operator note, leaving the brief intact |
| `description` | string | No | - | Replace the task title |
| `acceptance_criteria` | string | No | - | Replace the executor-facing brief |
| `priority` | integer | No | - | Requeue priority (higher drains first) |
| `execution_type` | string | No | - | agent \| pipeline \| a2a_task \| container \| human \| community |
| `required_capabilities` | array<string> | No | - | Capabilities an executor must match |
| `capability_match_strategy` | string | No | - | all \| any \| weighted |
| `delegation_config` | object | No | - | Delegation settings |

Hand a pending/in-progress Ralph task to a platform agent (A2A) instead of executing it yourself. Reuses spawn_task's capability-matrix + delegation-authority checks. With await, blocks until the agent finishes and records the outcome on the loop. No-op when halted.

| `timeout` | integer | No | - | Await timeout seconds (max 300) |
| `budget_cents` | integer | No | - | Budget for the delegated task |

| `params` | object | No | - | Query/path/body parameters for the endpoint |

### `data_source_subscribe`

Create or update a pull-based subscription to an endpoint (Ai::DataSourceSubscription). The server-side monitor polls due subscriptions on the given cadence, change-detects (etag/checksum), warms the cache and emits a data_source_changed signal on change. Requires ai.data_sources.stream.

| `params` | object | No | - | Query/path/body parameters passed to each poll |
| `poll_frequency` | string | No | - | Cadence: manual\|5min\|hourly\|daily\|weekly\|monthly\|realtime (default hourly) |

Remove a pull-based subscription. Provide subscription_id, or data_source_id + endpoint_id to remove the matching subscription(s). Requires ai.data_sources.stream.

| `endpoint_id` | string | No | - | Endpoint UUID or slug (with data_source_id) |

### `data_source_invalidate_cache`

Invalidate cached responses via Ai::DataSources::ResponseCacheService. With a tag, clears every entry under that surrogate key (ResponseCacheService.invalidate_by_tag). Otherwise clears by scope: data_source + endpoint_id clears that endpoint's variants, data_source alone clears all of the source's entries. Requires ai.data_sources.update (or .manage).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | No | - | Data source UUID or slug (required unless tag is given) |
| `endpoint_id` | string | No | - | Endpoint UUID or slug to scope the invalidation |
| `tag` | string | No | - | Surrogate cache tag (e.g. ds:<id>, endpoint:<id>, slug:<slug>); takes precedence over scope |

### `data_source_export`

Export a data source's CREDENTIAL-FREE config manifest via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#export (source + endpoints MINUS all secrets). The manifest carries the auth_scheme NAME and non-secret broker knobs only — never api keys, credentials, or secret auth_config values. Re-importable to recreate the source elsewhere.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | - | Data source UUID or slug |

### `data_source_import`

Import a CREDENTIAL-FREE config manifest into the account via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#import (create-or-update the source by slug, upsert endpoints by slug, all in one transaction). NEVER sets credentials — attach those separately after import. Requires ai.data_sources.create or .manage; agents lacking it file a proposal. Supports dry_run to preview the create/update plan without persisting.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `manifest` | object | Yes | - | Credential-free manifest (as produced by data_source_export) |
| `slug` | string | No | - | Override target source slug (clones under a new slug; name auto-deduped) |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | - | Preview the create/update plan without persisting (default false) |

List the built-in library of reusable, credential-free data-source templates (Ai::DataSources::TemplateLibrary). Each entry is a starter manifest for a well-known or generic source: slug, name, description, category.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

NEVER sets credentials — attach those afterward if the source requires auth. Requires ai.data_sources.create or .manage; agents lacking it file a proposal.

- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |

List a data source's append-only config-version history (Ai::DataSourceConfigVersion), latest first: version number, created_by_type (auto|manual|rollback), note, and created_at. Each row is a credential-free manifest snapshot captured by snapshot!/rollback.

Roll a data source's config back to a prior version via Ai::DataSources::ConfigPortabilityService#rollback! (captures the current state as a new 'rollback' snapshot first, then replays the historical manifest — credentials are never touched). Requires ai.data_sources.manage; agents lacking it file a proposal.

- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | - | Data source UUID or slug |
| `version` | integer | Yes | - | Config version NUMBER to restore |

### `data_source_reconcile`

DETERMINISTIC multi-source merge: governed-fetch every target (Ai::DataSources::QueryService) INDEPENDENTLY, collect each successful FetchEnvelope's records, then collapse them into one list by EXACT canonical-key match via Ai::DataSources::ReconciliationService (strategy first_wins|last_wins|merge). No cross-source SQL/join, no fuzzy entity resolution — exact key merge only. Requires ai.data_sources.query (it fetches). A write/side-effecting target endpoint additionally requires ai.data_sources.manage; without it, that target files a proposal instead of dispatching the live call. Returns the merged records plus per-source status.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `targets` | array<string> | Yes | - | Targets to fetch + merge; each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } |
| `key` | string | Yes | - | Canonical key field name shared across the sources |
| `strategy` | string | No | - | Merge strategy: first_wins\|last_wins\|merge (default last_wins) |
| `params` | object | No | - | Query params forwarded to EVERY target fetch |

### `data_source_failover_query`

Ordered FAILOVER across equivalent targets via Ai::DataSources::FailoverService#query: try each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } IN ORDER (primary first) through the full governed QueryService pipeline and return the FIRST success; if all fail, return the last failure envelope. Requires ai.data_sources.query. If ANY target is a write/side-effecting endpoint the agent lacks ai.data_sources.manage for, the whole call files a proposal instead of dispatching. Returns the winning FetchEnvelope with failover provenance (failover_used/failover_attempts/failover_source).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `targets` | array<string> | Yes | - | Ordered targets (primary first); each { data_source_id, endpoint_id } |
| `params` | object | No | - | Query params forwarded to every attempt |

### `data_source_replay`

Forensic, side-effect-free REPLAY of a recorded fetch via Ai::DataSources::ReplayService#replay: reconstruct a FetchEnvelope-shaped view from the redacted ai_data_source_queries audit row WITHOUT any network call, signing, or credential resolution. The cached body (when still present and the original params are supplied) is RE-MASKED for the current requester. Requires ai.data_sources.read.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `query_id` | string | No | - | ai_data_source_queries row UUID to replay |
| `correlation_id` | string | No | - | Fetch correlation id to replay |
| `params` | object | No | - | Original request params — supplied ONLY to recover the cached (re-masked) body |

### `data_source_ingest_to_kb`

RAG ingestion bridge: governed-fetch a source+endpoint (Ai::DataSources::QueryService) then pipe the canonical records into a knowledge base as embedded Ai::Document rows via Ai::DataSources::RagIngestionService#ingest (source_type "api", incremental re-embed dedup by record key). Requires ai.data_sources.manage (it writes documents/embeddings); agents lacking it file a proposal. Returns the ingest counts (ingested/updated/skipped/capped/errors).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::DataSourceTool`
- **Permission**: ai.data_sources.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `data_source_id` | string | Yes | - | Data source UUID or slug to fetch from |
| `endpoint_id` | string | Yes | - | Endpoint UUID or slug to fetch |
| `knowledge_base_id` | string | Yes | - | Target knowledge base UUID |
| `key` | string | No | - | Canonical record-key field for incremental re-embed dedup (optional) |
| `params` | object | No | - | Query/path/body parameters for the fetch |

| `entity_type` | string | Yes | - | Entity type: file, directory, class, module, method, function, variable, type_definition, interface, constant |
| `file_path` | string | No | - | File path relative to codebase root |
| `line_range` | string | No | - | Line range (e.g. '10-25') |
| `description` | string | No | - | Human-readable description |
| `properties` | object | No | - | Additional metadata |

### `code_create_relation`

Create a typed edge between two code nodes (e.g. imports, calls, inherits).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.knowledge_graph.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `source_node_id` | string | Yes | - | Source node ID |
| `target_node_id` | string | Yes | - | Target node ID |
| `relation_type` | string | Yes | - | Relation type: imports, calls, defines, inherits, implements, contains, related_to, depends_on, uses |
| `weight` | number | No | - | Edge weight 0-1 (default 1.0) |
| `properties` | object | No | - | Edge metadata |

### `code_search_graph`

Search the code graph with optional multi-hop traversal. Combines name matching with graph expansion.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.agents.read

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | - | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `query` | string | Yes | - | Search query |
| `entity_types` | array<string> | No | - | Filter by entity types |
| `max_depth` | integer | No | - | Graph traversal depth (default 2) |
| `top_k` | integer | No | - | Max results (default 10) |

### `code_prune_stale`

Find and remove/archive code nodes for files that no longer exist on disk (async — dispatched to the worker; result written to shared memory, retrieve via read_shared_memory). Use dry_run to preview.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.knowledge_graph.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | Yes | - | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `dry_run` | boolean | No | - | Preview without executing (default true) |

### `code_bulk_index`

Trigger codebase indexing (async — dispatched to the worker; returns immediately). Parses source files, creates knowledge graph nodes/edges, and generates embeddings. Track progress with code_index_status.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CodeMemoryTool`
- **Permission**: ai.knowledge_graph.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `repository_id` | string | No | - | Git repository ID, name, or full_name |
| `base_path` | string | No | - | Filesystem path to codebase root |
| `path` | string | No | - | Subdirectory to index (default: entire codebase) |
| `incremental` | boolean | No | - | Only re-index changed files (default true) |

## Improvement Campaigns

### `campaign_propose`

Propose a new improvement/feature CAMPAIGN into the discovery/delegation queue (deduped per target). Use THIS for any request to create, propose, or queue a CAMPAIGN — NOT the generic create_proposal (which is for agent change-proposals). Returns the proposal; approve it with campaign_approve_proposal to spawn the campaign.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Yes | - | Short proposal title |
| `objective` | string | Yes | - | What the campaign should accomplish |
| `source` | string | No | - | discovery\|trajectory\|improvement\|manual (default manual) |
| `scope` | string | No | - | Target/repo scope label (used for per-target dedupe) |
| `suggested_workload` | string | No | - | improvement-campaign\|feature-development\|new-project |
| `suggested_driver` | string | No | - | claude_code\|platform_agent\|platform_team\|platform_mission |
| `decision_authority` | string | No | - | supervised\|monitored\|trusted\|autonomous (default trusted) |
| `configuration` | object | No | - | Spawn configuration (scope/posture/plan_increments/...) |

### `campaign_list_proposals`

List the CAMPAIGN PROPOSAL QUEUE (the discovery/delegation control plane) for this account — the proposed/queued/approved/rejected/spawned campaign proposals awaiting review. Use THIS to answer 'what campaigns are proposed / in the discovery queue'.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | - | Filter: proposed\|queued\|approved\|rejected\|spawned |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max rows (default 50) |

### `campaign_update_proposal`

Revise a proposed/queued CampaignProposal's fields before it's approved — the operator-directed review-round counterpart to campaign_propose (which is for creating/rediscovery-refreshing). Errors if the proposal is already approved, rejected, or spawned. Recomputes the dedupe fingerprint when scope/objective/suggested_workload change. Only the fields you pass are updated.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `proposal_id` | string | Yes | - | CampaignProposal UUID |
| `title` | string | No | - | New proposal title |
| `objective` | string | No | - | New objective |
| `source` | string | No | - | discovery\|trajectory\|improvement\|manual |
| `scope` | string | No | - | New target/repo scope label |
| `suggested_workload` | string | No | - | improvement-campaign\|feature-development\|new-project |
| `suggested_driver` | string | No | - | claude_code\|platform_agent\|platform_team\|platform_mission |
| `decision_authority` | string | No | - | supervised\|monitored\|trusted\|autonomous |
| `configuration` | object | No | - | Replaces the proposal's spawn configuration |

### `campaign_approve_proposal`

Approve a queued/proposed proposal AND spawn its Ai::Campaign (and dev-loop) in one step — the concierge's 'create this campaign' action. Idempotent. Returns the proposal + the spawned campaign + its loop.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `proposal_id` | string | Yes | - | CampaignProposal UUID |

### `campaign_reject_proposal`

Reject a proposed/queued CampaignProposal — the operator decided not to pursue it. Terminal: a rejected proposal is never resurrected by a later campaign_propose rediscovery at the same fingerprint. Errors if already approved/rejected/spawned (use campaign_stop to stop an already-spawned campaign instead).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `proposal_id` | string | Yes | - | CampaignProposal UUID |
| `reason` | string | No | - | Why this proposal was rejected |

### `campaign_delegate`

Route a campaign's dev-loop to a driver — claude_code (a Claude Code session drains the pull queue) or platform_agent|platform_team|platform_mission (the platform executor drains it). Reassignment releases the current single-driver lease so the new driver can claim it; for claude_code, pass holder to take the lease immediately.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `driver_kind` | string | Yes | - | claude_code\|external_cli\|platform_agent\|platform_team\|platform_mission |
| `target` | object | No | - | Platform target ref: { agent_id\|group_id\|mission_id } |
| `holder` | string | No | - | Driver identity (claude_code: take the lease now) |

### `campaign_start`

Start an Autonomous Improvement Campaign: creates the campaign + a dedicated campaign-scoped Ralph loop that /dev-loop drains. Returns the campaign + loop.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Campaign name |
| `description` | string | No | - | Optional campaign description |
| `configuration` | object | No | - | scope/posture/ordering/keep-going |
| `decision_authority` | string | No | - | supervised\|monitored\|trusted\|autonomous |
| `stop_conditions` | object | No | - | e.g. { max_failed:, completion_pct: } |

### `campaign_list`

List this account's Autonomous Improvement CAMPAIGNS (spawned/active/completed), newest first. Use to answer 'what campaigns are running / exist'.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | - | Filter: created\|active\|paused\|completed\|archived |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max rows (default 50) |

### `campaign_status`

Live status: refreshes the ledger and returns the campaign summary, open parked questions, recent decisions, and its loops.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |

### `campaign_claim`

Become the single active driver for a campaign before driving it. Returns ok:true with the lease when acquired/renewed, or ok:false with held_by when another driver holds it (back off instead of double-driving the campaign/<id> branch).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `holder` | string | No | - | Driver identity (defaults to your user id) |

### `campaign_release`

Release a campaign's single-driver lease when done driving it.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `holder` | string | No | - | Driver identity (defaults to your user id) |

### `campaign_answer_question`

Answer a parked question (can unblock its associated task).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `question_id` | string | Yes | - | Parked question UUID |
| `answer` | string | Yes | - | The operator's answer to the parked question |

### `campaign_record_increment`

Record one completed campaign increment: marks a passed RalphTask on the campaign loop, logs a decision, and snapshots progress (so completion% reflects real work). Idempotent on task_key.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `title` | string | Yes | - | Short increment title |
| `summary` | string | No | - | What was done |
| `task_key` | string | No | - | Stable key for idempotency |
| `decision_type` | string | No | - | build\|unblock\|skip\|remove\|defer\|policy\|escalate (default build) |
| `rationale` | string | No | - | Why this increment was done / decided |
| `status` | string | No | - | passed (default) \| failed \| skipped |
| `check_results` | object | No | - | Verification evidence (e.g. {"rspec": "12 examples, 0 failures"}). A passed increment records checks_passed=true ONLY when this carries a green machine tally; without it the pass records as attested. |

### `campaign_check_rebase`

Advise the drivers of any open campaign whose branch is behind the target branch (default develop) that a rebase is needed — notifies them + flags likely conflicts. Run after a manual land or on a schedule (auto-lands trigger it automatically). Deduped per target tip.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `target_branch` | string | No | - | Target branch (default develop) |
| `exclude_campaign_id` | string | No | - | Campaign UUID to skip (e.g. the one just landed) |

### `campaign_stop`

Stop a campaign: pauses its loops (executors stop pulling) and marks it completed.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::CampaignTool`
- **Permission**: ai.campaigns.manage

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `campaign_id` | string | Yes | - | Campaign UUID or name |
| `summary` | string | No | - | Completion summary |

## Conversations & Workspaces

### `send_message`

Send a message to any conversation (workspace or agent). The conversation's agent will auto-respond (async for regular agents, sync for concierge). Include @mentions to notify specific agents in workspaces.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation ID (workspace or agent) |
| `message` | string | Yes | - | Message content (include @AgentName to mention) |
| `mentions` | array<string> | No | - | Structured agent mentions [{"id": "...", "name": "..."}] |

### `send_concierge_message`

Send a message to the Powernode concierge and get an AI response. Creates or reuses an active concierge conversation.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `message` | string | Yes | - | Message to send to the concierge |

### `confirm_concierge_action`

Confirm a pending concierge action (create_mission, delegate_to_team, code_review, deploy).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation ID containing the pending action |
| `action_type` | string | Yes | - | Action type: create_mission, delegate_to_team, code_review, deploy |
| `action_params` | object | No | - | Optional parameters (overrides original params) |

### `list_messages`

Retrieve messages from any conversation (workspace or agent)

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation ID |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max messages (default 20, max 100) |

### `get_conversation_messages`

Retrieve message history for a conversation including role, content, metadata, and timestamps

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation ID to retrieve messages from |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max messages to return (default 20, max 100) |

### `list_conversations`

List all conversations — workspaces, agent conversations, and concierge chats

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | - | Filter by status: active, paused, completed, archived (default: all) |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max results (default 10, max 50) |

### `list_workspaces`

List workspace conversations (alias for list_conversations filtered to workspaces)

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `status` | string | No | - | Filter by status: active, paused, completed, archived (default: all) |
| `limit` | integer | No | - | Max results (default 10, max 50) |

### `create_workspace`

Create a workspace conversation with selected agents for multi-agent collaboration.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | - | Workspace name |
| `agent_ids` | array<string> | No | - | Agent IDs to include |
| `include_concierge` | boolean | No | - | Auto-add concierge (default: false) |

### `invite_agent`

Invite an agent to a workspace conversation

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Workspace conversation ID |
| `agent_id` | string | Yes | - | Agent ID (or 'concierge') |

### `active_sessions`

List active MCP client sessions that can be invited to workspaces

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create
- **Parameters**: none

### `pin_conversation`

Pin a conversation to the top of the sidebar list. Sets pinned_at to now.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation UUID or conversation_id |

### `unpin_conversation`

Unpin a conversation (clears pinned_at).

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation UUID or conversation_id |

### `tag_conversation`

Set, add, or remove tags on a conversation. Pass `tags:` to replace, `add_tag:` to append, or `remove_tag:` to remove.

- **Tool class**: `Ai::Tools::ConversationTool`
- **Permission**: ai.conversations.create

| Parameter | Type | Required | Values | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `conversation_id` | string | Yes | - | Conversation UUID or conversation_id |
| `tags` | array<string> | No | - | Replace the conversation's tag list with this array |
| `add_tag` | string | No | - | Append a single tag (idempotent — won't dup) |
| `remove_tag` | string | No | - | Remove a single tag |
